problem: Holden has a collection of polygons. He writes down a list containing the measure of each interior angle of each of his polygons. He writes down the list $30^	ext{◦}$, $50^	ext{◦}$, $60^	ext{◦}$, $70^	ext{◦}$, $90^	ext{◦}$, $100^	ext{◦}$, $120^	ext{◦}$, $160^	ext{◦}$, and $x^	ext{◦}$, in some order. Compute $x$.
solution: We work in degrees. The sum of all $9$ angles is $680 + x$. The sum of the angles in a polygon with $n$ sides is $180(n - 2) \equiv 180n \mod 360$. Since there are $9$ angles, the polygons have a total of $9$ sides, so the sum of the $9$ angles must be $9 \times 180 \equiv 180 \mod 360$. Thus $680 + x \equiv 180 \mod 360$, so $x \equiv 220 \mod 360$. Since $0 < x < 360$, we know $x = 220$.
